For years now there’s been something drawing you to the quiet darkness of an otherwise empty forest outpost. There are critical elements to this interest though which are non-negotiable - it they’re not present, then the entire vibe is thrown off and it doesn’t work.

First and foremost is rain sounds. You knew the moment you heard the sounds of rain as the ship passed Saturn in Interstellar that it’s the sound that relaxes you most - the sounds that drowns out the other noise, any intrusive thoughts you might have, and never distracts you in itself. Right now you’ve got the Dark Forest Ambient Focus Music from YouTube on the other screen as you type, and the ambient synths are a fraction distracting… but the rain sounds that run underneath help make up for it.

item.title: Mini Essay - Appeal of living out of a van
item.description: One of the ideas that has stuck with me for decades now is the idea of living alone out of a van. I had the opportunity to do it when I went to Iceland in 2016, and it’s always stuck with me as a wonderful but slightly dislocated existence - like I knew I enjoyed having everything in my car and being free to go anywhere at any time, but not feeling like I could really stop anywhere either.

item.title: Mini Essay - Appeal of Small
item.description:
There’s something uniquely engaging about the world of the small. Whether it’s plastic WH40k miniatures, bonsai trees, LEGO, tilt-shift photography, ant colonies, model railways, or any one of a dozen other examples, there’s something that hooks the attention of many people in a way that the full scale version doesn’t.

Part of me thinks this may be a predominantly masculine trait, especially when I think things like toy soldiers and action figures, but then I only need to think of Barbie and Polly Pocket to realise that this particular focus on the world of the small isn’t really gendered - it’s just that we more often see men with hobbies that lend themselves to small things.

item.title: Mini Essay - Appeal of Thronglets
item.description: For some time I’ve wanted to rewatch the “Plaything” episode of Black Mirror with the express intent of zeroing in on why there’s so much appeal in an evolving digital sentience. On the surface the thronglets are terrifying - a digital lifeform that might be initially dismissed as an addictive game that’s hooked a vulnerable and emotionally overwhelmed man who took acid and became convinced the thronglets were talking to him, but they’re revealed at the end to be exactly as powerful and intelligent as he claimed when an audio signal rewrites the brains of everyone who hears it.

item.title: Mini Essay - April 19 (2023)
item.description:
Mini Essay - April 19 (2026)

I want to preface this by saying I wasn’t expecting to write it, and I’ve been working for the last few days on an entirely different and unrelated post about how I’m preparing for Mars One selection later this year. I’ll still publish that post in the next few days, but I’m not sure if I’ll publish this outside of Patreon. Maybe next year. Truth be told I may not publish this at all – all I know is I just realised what the date is, it stopped me in my tracks, and I need to write this right down while I’m feeling what I’m feeling.

item.title: Mini Essay - Before You're 40
item.description:
With just three months away, it’s suddenly becoming a big and urgent question of what you want to do before you’re 40, and more importantly what kind of life you want to live in your 40’s. You never really thought you’d make it to 30, and yet here you are nearly 10 years later wondering what you want to do next.

You 40s really need to be about embracing the life you want to live and reinforcing those things you love most. There’s no question you love writing books on your own, thinking deeply about difficult things, and sharing experiences with others who would never do see what you see without you. Your 40s should be about being bolder in the things you excel at, and cutting free the things that drag. All the philosophy you want to live by is already within you, already hashed out in your notes - now if the time to live it fully.

item.title: Mini Essay - Before You're 50
item.description: For the last few months since I turned 40, I’ve been trying to reassess my life and all the things I’ve done so far with limited success. Much of the challenge has come from knowing just how much there is to sort through and reframe, coupled with having ignored my writing for so long that it feels like there’s a kind of psychic constipation built-up - my recent writing is easing that pressure, but there is a whole lot clogged up that needs to be processed while still more builds up behind it.

item.title: Mini Essay - Choosing between potential jobs
item.description: Right now you’re looking at two different job opportunities, and both of them offer different elements of what you’re looking for in a career in cyber. It’s also important to remember that you don’t need either of these roles - they’re the first to come back to you, and they’ve both provided you with 2nd interviews today, but that doesn’t mean that either of them is the right fit for you - only that they’re the things that are being offered this week.

item.title: Mini Essay - Desires from work and a career in cyber
item.description: To determine what you want from work and your career in cybersecurity more generally, you really need to go back to why you got into cyber in the first place. This whole journey started because you were looking for work that was IT-related, because you haven’t never worked in IT have an aptitude for it. Your initial investigations were leading you down the Gaming pathway - that’s why you spoke to Martin about his work as much as you did, and why you bought a couple of cheap courses in modelling/gaming design in Unity. The interest in working with computers came first, and then the specialisation.

item.title: Mini Essay - Digital Garden
item.description:
First #mini-essay

While the internet has been overwhelmingly consumed with a “feed” or “stream” style where information and opinions are delivered as an unalterable fact, the early days of the internet were far more collaborative and interwoven.

The earliest web pages behaved much like a digital “garden” rather than a feed or chronological blog - posts and snippets of information being woven together in a dense tapestry that was always evolving and interlinking. While a feed provides the most recent and “important” content at the top, a digital garden provides a wide array of entry points and no two journey’s through it are the same. For the last 20 years the internet has evolved into a broad array of feeds all vying for the attention of visitors, delivering the latest and greatest at all times.

item.title: Mini Essay - Dune
item.description: For years now I’ve felt this overwhelming connection to the Dune universe, and in many ways that connection has felt as undefinable as the series itself. Some might refer to the “vibe” of Dune being appealing, but for me there’s something more than just enjoying the aesthetic - it’s the whole body understanding that if you stop moving, if you try to stay in one place, to put up defences, to block the flow of energy… then you’ll be destroyed and swept away regardless.

item.title: Mini Essay - Fear Is The Mind Killer
item.description:
“Fear is the mind killer” is the most easily recognised line from the “Litany Against Fear” from the Dune universe. Recited by high-born characters in times of high stress or when death threatens, it acts to centre and stabilise the emotions of those who recited it through the application of cold logic.

Accepting fear and allowing it to pass over you is vital to remaining in control when it could take control of your mind. In the universe of Dune, the litany is adopted as a vaccine to a digital virus that feeds on fear. However it’s origin can be traced back to Act II of Shakespeare’s Julius Caesar, in a quote which has been adapted numerous times - most notably paraphrased as “A coward dies a thousand deaths, but the brave die only once”.

item.title: Mini Essay - First Day in Ushuaia
item.description: It’s your first day in Ushuaia and you’re naturally shattered from not sleeping in the last 2.5 days, but you’re managing well considering that. You definitely got a good feel for this place though, enough that you certainly reached a point earlier where you were tired, hungry and sore, and the magic of being so close to Antarctica (with the matching weather) had worn off and you just wanted to stop.

item.title: Mini Essay - Greatest moments of joy in your life
item.description:
Ask yourself what the greatest moments of life have been in your life so far? There are a few that standout

  • Finishing the fireman’s carry for your fitness assessment to leave Hunter Company.
  • Turning around on the top of Uhuru Peak on Mt Kilimanjaro.
  • Seeing the Northern Lights through the windshield in Norway.
  • Popping out into the Garden in Englebrecht’s East.
  • Your first dive in Downstream Slot Cave.
  • Having a wombat try to steal Russ.
  • Being awarded the Golden Compass
  • Rescuing an echidna from L301
  • Finding downstream L301
  • Meeting Alex Alexakis in Adelaide
  • Passing my Security+
  • Passing my AZ-500
  • Finding the link between the White room and The Wedge Room in Pines
  • Looking through the One Tree swim-through for the first time
  • Your first breath underwater with a rebreather
  • Being selected for the Mars 100
  • Discovering Mars One
  • Diving Silfra
  • Setting fire to the koala suit
  • Holding a baby wombat on Flinders Island
  • The Becoming Martian book launch
  • Seeing the Lemurs at the Calgary Zoo
  • Joining the Ginger Pride parade in Melbourne
  • Seeing a Saturn V at Cape Canaveral
  • Watch Felix Baumgartner jump out of the Red Bull capsule
  • Eating a pie and drinking strawberry milk at the end of Ex Talisman Sabre

References

item.title: Mini Essay - Handwritten journal vs going digital
item.description: There’s no question that writing has played an absolutely vital role in your development since you first discovered Mars One in September 2012. It took awhile for you to figure out how you wanted to do this, but handwritten journals have formed the mainstay for more than a decade. In the last few years though, you’ve noticed your journaling drop right off, with regular gaps ever since 2020 and the COVID nightmare. You were working so hard on Cosmic Nomad that you poured out your heart and mind into that book, leaving no desire or need to then write by hand in a journal. And the reality is you’ve never really picked that up properly since.

item.title: Mini Essay - If Mars One rebooted
item.description: For some time you’ve been aware that the shutdown of Mars One in 2020 has left you very adrift and directionless in the world, and one of the questions that’s come up repeatedly is what you’d do if Mars One suddenly rebooted. Bas floated the idea when the Ridley Scott documentary was first being discussed, but we’ve heard nothing on that for well beyond the 12 month exclusivity contract. But the question remains - what would you do if Mars One rebooted tomorrow?

item.title: Mini Essay - If you had a year to live
item.description: If you knew you were going to die in a year, what would you do? Would you stay at work? Fuck no. Would you stay here with Chloe? Maybe, but only if it were to write as much as you possibly could with your final year. If you were going to die before you turned 41, there’s no question you’d travel and write constantly. And you certainly wouldn’t be diving in Mt Gambier - you’d be going straight to Spain to cave dive, maybe France for more of the same.

item.title: Mini Essay - Kids Meals on Planes
item.description:
Topic: Kids Meals on Planes

I’d never realised it before, but every meal on a plane is basically a kids meal. I’ve just visited my relentlessly obnoxious 3 year old nephew, and on the flight back to Adelaide I’ve been served focaccia topped with chorizo, pesto, bell peppers & goats cheese. Seems fancy as fuck, but looking at the box it was served in I realised it’s just like what you’d pull out of a Happy Meal. And that’s the trick, isn’t it? We’re being served little boxes of snacks to keep us happy as we fly through space in an aluminium tube full of recycled farts.

item.title: Mini Essay - Letter to Yourself in 2031
item.description:
Where do I want to be in 5 Years time?

Dear Josh in 2031, Firstly I hope you’re still around to read this. Given the way your life has changed through the years, you’ve gone through plenty of period where you didn’t think you’d make it another 5 years. So if you’re reading this, nice work - you made it!

You’ll be 45 when you’re reading this and a about a month and a half away from your 46th birthday. Right now 46 doesn’t feel as significant at 45 does, in much the same way 40 didn’t feel as significant as I think 42 will be. You’ll have been diving for 34 years, with the last 2 of them cave diving. You’ll also have a decade of Cyber Security experience if you’re still doing it, which seems pretty uncertain right now. You’ve just started work with Alpha Echo after a bumpy 6-8 months leaving ElectraNet, going to Sulawesi and Antarctica, breaking up with Chloe, living in a Van, moving in with Simone, and asking a lot of questions about who or what you want to be.

item.title: Mini Essay - MechWarrior
item.description:
There’s something really unique about my life-long relationship with the BattleTech / MechWarrior videogame series. The tabletop game look interesting too, but I’ve never really gone in for tabletop wargames except to paint them as models. But the videogames have always held a very special place in my heart, and it goes all the way back to my first exposure through MechWarrior 2.

Being able to stop around in such a huge bipedal robot and shoot things has to be a huge part of this. The idea of controlling a building size walking machine fitted with lasers and rockets is certainly awe inspiring, far more than I’d feel driving a tracked vehicle. In fact the tracked and flying vehicles in MechWarrior 5 often feel out of place when I see them in-game - more like a machine and less like a powerful giant.

item.title: Mini Essay - Mental Baggage
item.description: One of my ongoing challenges is keeping track of and managing all the different things that engage my attention. This can mean my Personal, asking Mini Essay - What are your obligations, my Work, and anything else that contacts my senses and hooks my attention. While I can track a wide range of interests and passions, the real challenge for me is task-switching: being invested in one thing, but needing to keep something else in mind at the same time, or being pulled away from my focus to handle some other issue.

item.title: Mini Essay - New Tattoo
item.description:
Getting a new tattoo has been a consideration for several years now, however there’s been some hesitation over what, where, and why.

The design that I’ve circled back to repeatedly is from the Zen Pencils comic for George Mallory’s “Because It’s There” quote, specifically from the cell where the Inventor is climbing with the text “We eat and make money to be able to live”. So much of what I’ve done for the last 15 years (and even earlier if I’m honest) has been about doing things that make me feel alive, and doing them regardless of whether other people understand the motivation.

item.title: Mini Essay - Not Fade Away (Jim Dodge)
item.description:
“Not Fade Away” turned out to be quite an interesting read after the initial confusion around the book by Ben Torres-Fong of the same name (accidentally read first before realising the author was different>. There’s no way I would have read it unless it had been on the 101 Things - Complete List list, but that’s the case with so many of those books anyway.

The narrative within a narrative was interesting, and was something that was easy to forget when I was in the thick of George’s story and not realising what I was reading was being told by George to someone else. Besides “Zen and the Art of Motorcycle Maintenance” I’ve not read an “on the road” book like it before, and a lot of it felt like going places just to go there, not to actually do anything. Even the idea of burning the Big Bopper’s car seemed arbitrary - it really was just about the journey in the end, and the people you meet along the way.

item.title: Mini Essay - November 23
item.description:
Related:

In early January 2010, I was on Dartmoor doing a survival exercise with the Royal Marine Commandos. I’d been training with them for a few months, and somewhere between the days of trudging through 6ft of soft snow and shivering through the -20°C nights, I was bitten by a deer tick. I didn’t know at the time that I’d been infected with Lymes disease, but 5 weeks later I was admitted to CTCRM’s hospital where I lost 8 kg in 5 days and nearly died.

item.title: Mini Essay - Now You're 40
item.description: Turning 40 hasn’t had any obvious impact on me so far, at least not in the way that turning 30 did as I discussed in Mini Essay - Why you didn’t think you’d make it to 30. I still joke about not living particularly long because of the stuff I do while cave diving, but the last 10 years haven’t had the same edge to them that the previous 10 did. As I’ve written elsewhere, I think being involved with Mars One made me think about where I’d be in 10 years time (eg. on my way to mars) rather than where I’d be when I turned a particular age.

item.title: Mini Essay - Organising a Mars One Analog
item.description:
An unexpected idea that appeared recently is to organise a Mars analog with a bunch of Mars One candidates in Wadi Rum. I’m not sure why something like this wasn’t organised previously, but the contact from DIrk through LinkedIn has triggered a cascade of ideas around a filmed Mars analogue featuring folks who volunteered for Mars One.

Thinking about it, it hasn’t taken much to put together a list of candidates to approach, or to pick a potential time to go - Jan/Feb 2027. There may be climate issues with a simulation in Wadi Rum then, but that’s all information you can research and put together before reaching out to potential analog astronauts. It’s also possible that 2027 is too soon, but I need to pick something to aim for, and it can always be adjusted later.

item.title: Mini Essay - Peaceful Warrior vs the Alchemist
item.description:
Having just finished two of the Peaceful Warrior books as well as the Alchemist, it feels like the perfect opportunity to compare and contrast the two in order to figure out what it is that makes them so special.

The stand out element from this most recent re-reading is that the Alchemist feels like an important reminder of the basics, whereas there are elements of the Peaceful Warrior series that seem new even though you’ve read it more than a dozen times. This time around rereading the Peaceful Warrior felt more important than the Alchemist, and I guess this is the opportunity to figure out why.

item.title: Mini Essay - Procrastinating Writing the Pines Article
item.description:
What’s the holdup on writing the article about your Crazy Wombat Tunnel discovery in Pines? You announced it all 2.5 months ago now, and yet you’ve never dedicated yourself to actually sitting down and writing something very important. Is this just procrastination, or is there something else here?

It’s easy to generate a list of excuses for not having done it yet - you’ve been sick, work has been full-on, you’ve been very focused on CISSP study, you’ve been dealing with the stress around Chloe wanting a home loan… is that it? It doesn’t feel like you’ve had many weekends to yourself, and the last weekend you had was dedicated to developing your Expedition plans (which you made excellent progress on).

item.title: Mini Essay - Ridiculous Bucket List
item.description: For the last few years I’ve had the idea of not just a bucket list, but a “ridiculous bucket list” - a list of things that seem utterly outrageous and infeasible, but the likes I would embrace in a heartbeat if the opportunity presented. While my bucket list includes things seeing an erupting volcano or joining the mile-high club, my ridiculous bucket list would have things like “Visit the Moon” and “Discover evidence for alien life on Mars”.

item.title: Mini Essay - Secret to dealing with work
item.description:
Related:

Surviving any uncomfortable workplace always requires an evil secret plan on your part, and your current situation is no different.

Your secret is that you’re using them as a stepping stone to more suitable work, and as a way to gain useful experience from both a corporate and technical perspective. From a technical perspective you’re now working in threat intelligence for a critical infrastructure organisation, which looks incredible on your resume. Being able to string those things together means you’re well on your way to choosing the kind of work you want in industries that you feel are important.

item.title: Mini Essay - Thoughts on 2025 Media
item.description:
Kindle

Not Fade Away (Jim Dodge) I have to laugh about this book because it’s on the 101 Things book list, but I accidentally read all of “Not Fade Away” by Ben Torres-Fong (about the early years of Rolling Stone) and didn’t realise I’d read the wrong book until I went to tick it off the list. I enjoyed both, but this one was certainly a lot weirder and more entertaining. It took me awhile to figure out that the journey was just an excuse to meet weird and wonderful characters along the way, but once I recognised that it was easy to settle in and see wherever the author decided to take it. Reading it wasn’t life changing, but it was certainly a fun read.

item.title: Mini Essay - Using my folding keyboard while flying from Melbourne to Santiago
item.description: I’ve just started my journey to Antarctica, or more accurately I’ve started the first overseas step to Antarctica with the flight from Melbourne to Santiago, and I’m getting used to working on the small Bluetooth keyboard I bought to avoid my laptop. This trip will be the first major test of this, not only learning to use a small form keyboard like this, but also the experience of travelling without a laptop - something I haven’t done since I left the marines.

item.title: Mini Essay - What are your obligations
item.description: As I put together the final things ready for the next few weeks in Antarctica and then Perth, I’m asking myself what my outstanding obligations are. This can be my emotional obligations (like people and things I feel I owe something to), physical obligations (like things that I have and feel responsible for), and my own spiritual obligations (the things that I feel I need to work on or do to feel fulfilled).

item.title: Mini Essay - What do you really want to do before you die
item.description: What do you really want to do before you die? It’s a tough question, and one that’s even tougher to contemplate. You’re 40 in a few months, which is wild considering you never thought you’d make it to 30. Now you talk about being lucky to make 70… maybe you need to ask yourself why you didn’t think you’d make it to 30, as well as what you’d do if you made it to 80 and have another 40 years of life ahead of you.

item.title: Mini Essay - What is fear to you
item.description:
This morning you spent a lot of time thinking during your walk about what fear means to you. There were a lot of examples, but actually pinning it down felt really hard, and much of that comes down to it being similar to distinctively different to anxiety.

For me, fear is cold followed by force. Fear is something you tend to run at, something you feel and immediately react to with action. Fear isn’t the every day concerns of things not working out or of something hypothetically happening - that’s anxiety. Fear is trying to hold a door closed as three sailors smash into it from the other side to kill you and rape the two women in the room with you. Fear is grabbing the fire extinguisher off the wall and breaking the toes in the foot jammed in the same door. Fear is holding onto a plastic sheet carrying a friend as they’re dying of hypothermia, as you run through the mud to get him into the back of an ambulance, then someone to help peel your fingers from the plastic because your hand has cramped onto it. Fear is going back to camp afterwards and finding two more, and knowing there’s no one left to help but you. Fear is talking your Mum through all the things she needs to put in a Go-Bag, because you’re sure that your father is going to try and kill her. Fear is begging her not to wait until he breaks in one night, to leave and get out now. Fear is him finding out where she’s been hiding, and having him threaten to fly across the country to kill her as well as my sister and her family too. Fear is knowing exactly what you’d to him do if he ever did.

item.title: Mini Essay - Where do I want to be in 2028
item.description:
There’s no denying that the last few months have been pretty turbulent, and I have a whole series of fairly significant life changes heading my way in the next month too. My perspective on life has massively shifted since turning 40 in August, leaving ElectraNet in September, and especially since Trip - Antarctica - 2025 Nov so it’s natural to look ahead and wonder where I’m trying to go next.

While everyone seems to put a lot of focus on turning 40, having drinks with Cairo last night reminded me that I’m still a massive Htchhikers Guide to the Galaxy nerd so I’ve always been more curious about what my life would look like at age 42. I’ll hit that milestone in August 2027, so I’m really curious about what my life is going to look like 4 months after that in 2028.

item.title: Mini Essay - Why Antarctica is Important to you
item.description:
As you sit in the airport at Buenos Aires after such a hefty few days of flying, it’s starting to really dawn on me that I’m about to flying to Ushuaia - the gateway to Antarctica. And in just a few days, I’ll be getting onboard an expedition ship Going to the Antarctic Peninsula!

There’s a big part of me that is simply not processing that fact - that in a few days I’ll be in Antarctica. I’m not sure if it’s the numbness you’ve experienced a lot of these last few years, but it’s not clear if my lack of excitement is because I haven’t come to terms with the reality of the trip yet, or if I’m downplaying it all in an attempt to protect my psyche from potential disappointment.

item.title: Mini Essay - Why I'm writing a book about cave diving
item.description: Writing a book about cave diving isn’t just the “right thing to do”, it’s also something I genuinely love the idea of doing. Writing is a huge part of my life and how I process things over time, and Diving is equally important to me having been part of my life for nearly 30 of my 40 years now. Cave diving is something that I’m fiercely passionate about and incredibly invested in, so it makes sense that I’d be drawn to the idea of combining these interests into writing a book about cave diving, especially if I put it in the context of my first 500 cave dives.

item.title: Mini Essay - Why it's easy to put off writing
item.description:
Related:

One of the challenges I routinely face is trying to prioritise writing as a regular practice. or as any kind of practice, regular or not. I know that I love writing, and even as I type this I can feel that sense of creation that I truly crave whenever I sit down and start typing out my thoughts on a keyboard - a particularly visceral experience where each click of the keyboard is another step towards an artistic expression that’s yearning to be shared.

item.title: Mini Essay - Why you didn't think you'd make it to 30
item.description: Throughout most of my 20’s I was certain I wouldn’t be alive to turn 30. It’s not like I can pinpoint exactly where that idea came from, but there’s no question it was a recurring belief that shaped the way I thought and planned my life. If I try to trace it back, I suspect I’ll wind up back at April 19th, 2008. I made a choice that night to live, and it was certainly a close-call, but I’ve used that night as a reference for most of my life since - no matter what awful shit I’ve been through since then, I know that I will never allow myself to be trapped in that mindset ever again, where suicide felt like the only way out.

item.title: Mini Essay - Your Cave Diving Future
item.description: Now that you’ve been suspended by the CDAA, you have an amazing opportunity to look ahead and ask what kind of future you want to have in cave diving. You knew the suspension was coming, and you’ve been more than emotionally ready to tackle it - part of you has even relished it finally coming to pass. So the question now is how you want to develop as an exploration cave diver outside of Mt Gambier and the CDAA.

item.title: Mini Essay - Your evil secret plan
item.description: Ask yourself “What is your evil secret plan?”. Ultimately this is a question about how you’re going to use the system to do the things that YOU want to do and live the life you want to live. We’re not talking about blindly trying to “Live your dreams” - we’re talking about gaming the system so it looks like you’re playing along with everyone else, but you’re hacking the game so you do exactly what you want regardless of what others may expect or even demand of you. So you’re not playing by any rules, but you are faking compliance while you put all the pieces into place to subvert expectations.

item.title: Note - Mini Essays
item.description:
Original: https://youtu.be/N4YjXJVzoZY

Short piece of writing on some thing you find interesting All about retention, learning & reflection Write fast and often - over time it provides depth Mini-essays make learning more addictive by being novel Like a sketchbook for an artist

Three rules of Mini-essays

  1. Only cover one idea
  2. Keep them short (fit on monitor without scrolling)
  3. Keep them organised (Obsidian)

Elements of mini-essay

  • 100-300 words (no scrolling within Obsidian, focus on being brief)
  • Storytelling approach? Prose? Make sure this serves your goals
  • Write it as if you’re teaching it (Feynmann technique)
  • Restrict to single concept (one distinct idea) or idea (save connection/blending for larger writing)

item.title: Patreon - Speaking for Free
item.description:
from email 2018-02-27

Over the last two years I’ve had a couple of fairly nasty experiences with friends and colleagues asking me to speak at their STEM event.

My general rule for the last few year has been to charge everyone booking me to speak, even if it’s just a small amount, because as soon as money is involved everyone (schools in particular) take things much more seriously. When they’re paying for your time, people make sure the presentation room is ready for you, the projector is working, and the kids are prepped. Teachers get their shit together when something is coming out of their budget, and because they’re so focused on doing their jobs they also tend to dismiss anything they’re getting for free. Zero dollars, zero investment.

item.title: Website – 101 Things (79 Speed Dating) The Mighty Ginge
item.description: College Of Awesome – 101 Things (#79 Speed Dating) As much as it pains me to admit it – it’s Valentine’s Day tomorrow. And while last week’s Ron Burgundy Day tried to get the sex back into sexual harassment, there’s still plenty of people out there turning to Valentine’s Day for some old-fashioned commercialised romance. So instead of raging any further about the dubious history of St. Valentine’s Day, I’d like to suggest an alternative for those of you that failed to get laid from yelling “I WANT TO BE ON YOU” last week – speed dating. Now speed dating has a fair nasty stigma – dozens of guys and girls having “mini-dates” of 3-5 minutes, then ticking a secret ballot paper to say who they’d like to share contact details with – could be seen as slightly sleazy. But as someone who went speed dating at university (and had a damn good time doing it), I discovered it’s all in how you approach it. Most people went trying to meet the love of their life – I went to mess with other single people, and met a girl I lived with for 2 years. So if you are considering going speed dating to help numb the loneliness tomorrow, I have a few suggestions to turn what could be an uncomfortable and ultimately disappointing experience (and that’s just the cry-wank you have when you get home), into a few hours of random/memorable hilarity. Hell, you might even get laid out of it… Go For A Laugh, Not A Lay Sure, it’s got “dating” on the end of it – but who said speed dating has to be about romance? I went because A) The girl organising it is an old friend, B) She’d had someone drop out last-minute and need even numbers of guys to girls, and C) I thought it would be hilarious trying to convince every girl I met that I was born in the Andes and raised by mountain goats till I was 5. I had no intention of trying to meet someone – I’d just started my last year of university, was president of the most infamous social club on campus, and my project supervisor had just  vaporised without warning over the summer to another university. This was purely to help out a friend and have a laugh at the expense of others – the signs of a true gentleman. Go speed dating to meet crazy people, or just people in general. Go and see if you can convince someone you have a psychic link to spider monkeys (or lemurs in my case). Take a friend and dare each other to tell more and more elaborate lies. Just don’t go planning to meet the Captain of the SS Loveboat during a date shorter than most songs. Unless of course you’re telling people you are the Captain of the SS Loveboat, in which case please continue. I’m sure it’ll help you to… Be Memorable You’re about to meet more than a dozen members of the opposite sex, and you have 3-5 minutes to make a decision if you’d want them to call you. This is some high-pressure decision-making – fuck up and you could wind up inviting the girl who eats her toenails around for dinner with your parents, or sleeping with the guy who collects your hair for his extensive home-made doll collection. So you want to make a fast and memorable impression. But because you’re not trying to get them to home with you, you don’t need to stress about making a good impression. Of the 20 girls there, I remember just 4 of them; - The crazy blonde chick, who grabbed my ballot paper the moment I sat down and drew a cartoon elephant yelling “WEE-OR!” - The hockey-worshipping Canadian - The American who’d grown up in Indonesia and come to support the Canadian - The cranky brunette who I met last, spilt my drink on, and about 3 seconds before the night ended discovered had a shared interest in hiking. I have no idea if these were the most attractive/sweetest/most appropriate potential partners out of all the women there – all I know is they were the most interesting and memorable. The Canadian and American had it relatively easy because obviously being foreign alone made them more distinctive/memorable. And the cranky brunette was memorable simply because she was such a sour bitch. Sure, it was the end of the night and everyone had kind of had enough. And yes, I’d drunk enough to tranquillise a bull elephant by that stage. But scowling at someone on a 3 minute date? If I wanted to get judgemental glares from attractive women while I was drunk, I’d have started turning up to my psychology tutorials again. No, the really interesting one here is the blonde that drew the elephant. Now it’s not deliberate discrimination, but I have to admit I’ve never really been attracted to blonde women – my mum is blonde, and most of my friends in school were blonde girls and have always stayed friends. I’ve met a few “hot blondes” since leaving high school, but it was really the brunettes and redheads that kick-started this puberty party. So cartoon-elephant-drawing blonde girl was already heading into the friend zone before I’d sat down – that non-existent friend-zone I was using because I was just there for my own twisted amusement. But I distinctly remember her: even though she was one of the girls I met early in the night six years ago, and I’ve never had any contact with her again; I remember her because grabbing someone’s ballot paper and drawing a yelling cartoon elephant on it is a completely mental thing to do. I want to point out of course the elephant was the one yelling “WEE-OR!”, not her. But in retrospect I probably would have shared my details with her if she  had yelled “WEE-OR!” during our 3 minute date, because god knows that one would have been a keeper. Get Your Drunk On Alcohol – the cause and solution to all of the world’s problems. Sure, cranky-hiking-brunette didn’t appreciate me cheekily slurring and spilling my precious Southern Comfort everywhere – but if I hadn’t been drunk when I met her, I probably would have told her how absurdly dull she was. And I sure as shit wouldn’t have remembered her. So in this case alcohol stopped me from being rude to someone and helped me remember who they were. I’d highly recommend having a few drinks through the night, but maybe pace yourself. Remember you’re looking at 2-3 hours of social lubrication here. So when you have a break “to go to the bar” at the hour mark, maybe order a soft drink instead of the round of tequila shots I did. Maybe don’t start drinking 3 hours before “for courage”. And maybe don’t start stealing the drinks of your dates to “check for poison” because you’re not being a modern-day gentleman, your paving the way to rehab. Other than that, go out and have fun! Speed dating is a real blast – you’ll meet some fascinating people and have lots of laughs. And make sure you have lots of laughs. item.title: Website – How to Ruin Christmas
item.description: This is the final post of the year. The Mighty Ginge will be on break until January 17th,2011 –looking forward to seeing you all next year with new site features and new posts. Merry Christmas,and try to avoid killing yourselves over the New Year. The Mighty Ginge Task Ruin the annual yule-tide festivities through a series of increasingly disrespectful and socially-misguided acts. Background Christmas –a time to share with friends,family and reindeer. It’s the season for togetherness,appreciating those close to you,for generosity and empathy. It’s also the time of the year when people go batshit insane. Shopping,dinners,cards,letters –people are travelling and sending shit everywhere. They get together with family because “they have to”,put up with Grandad’s violent,racist and mysoginistic outbursts for the sake of “harmony”,send out bulk emails to people they don’t even talk to,break the bank buying gifts for kids who play with the box instead,and then take them to sit on the knee of some red-suited paedophile who talks about the goodies in his sack that he’ll give them if they’re good. So in response to this insanity,I’ve compiled a variety of ways you can strike back at the spirit of Saint Nic. These are merely suggestions and guidelines based on previous experiences however –I strongly encourage you all to create or recount your own misadventures,and post them in the comments below. Hitting the Fat Man where it hurts Disclaimer:As this is an entry level experience,I recommend starting out here for those looking to ruin their first Christmas. If at the end you feel any emotion other than malicious joy,I would recommend avoiding any of the other techniques and simply continuing to be passive aggressive at Christmas dinner when passing the salt. “Hitting the Fat Man”requires a high visibility and very large inflatable Santa Claus. Ideally the giant Santa will be located somewhere with limited physical access,but with massive visual impact –for example on the top of a shopping centre facing a freeway. You will need; - A lightweight ladder (or mad ninja skills) - A large,plain white sheet - Black spraypaint - Two bricks - Several meters of string. On Christmas eve,approach your target Santa from low ground below the sight line of any security cameras/roving patrols,and get access to the roof. This can either be by lifting yourself on the edge of a doorframe in a loading bay,hanging off the external grate of a nearby airvent and then swinging your legs onto the roof to pull yourself up backwards (eg. Generally being Sam Fisher);or bringing a ladder with you. Ensure though that you can pull the ladder onto the roof with you if you do use it though,least it be spotted by a roaming security guard. Once on the roof,tie the string to the corners of the sheet and use the bricks to hold the string in place,spreading the sheet out along the wall facing the freeway under Santa’s feet. Now spraypaint “SANTA ISN’T REAL –MERRY XMAS”in foot tall letters on the white sheet,climb back down the ladder/airvent,and make your escape. Chances are it will stay up there for 3 days,because the shopping centre needs to hire an elevated work platform to legally access that part of the roof. The Facade Breaker Extended family:you can’t pick them,but you can ensure they never speak to you again. Christmas with big families is usually a fairly stressful event for everyone,so save yourself the trouble of false pre tense and feigned respect –tell them what you think of them. For example if you’re 8 and having Christmas at your Grandad’s,playing with a water hose and enjoying a hot Australian summer,and he suddenly comes out of the kitchen with a carving knife in his hand screaming that you’ll kink the hose –tell your parents you’re scared of him (like the rest of the family),and that you won’t come out of a spider-infested caravan until he dies or they take you home. Alternatively,inform your parents every year that you’d rather be raped by a thousand angry Squirrel monkeys that see extended family for Christmas. When they finally do convince you that 5 days in a holiday home with them is survivable,give it a real chance. Stay quiet when the pointed questions about your career start;play the game when plans get changed at the last minute to suit the selfish needs of a few;bite your tongue when your the relatives start getting overly religious –it’s okay,your time will come. Because on Christmas night –when everyone is gathered around having a roast and your god-bothering Aunty steps up her week long campaign of bitchiness by accusing your Mum of trying to steal her children away –you get to step up and tell her to “stop acting like such a fucking child”,and that “everyone is sick of your shit”. When she demands you respect her because she’s your aunty,inform her that you respect people who deserve it (eg. not middle aged women who act like children),then storm out of the house. If your not sure that will get you cut off from family Christmases,make sure you rub salt in the wound by apologising to your aunt the next morning for the language you used,but make a point that you still think she’s acts like child and that you don’t care if she thinks it’s disrespectful,she can still fuck off. Seriously,let that shit out –a little work early on will save you a lifetime of awkward Christmas conversations and annual attempts to justify yourself to people you don’t like just because you share genetic material. Spread the Malice Just because you’ve been banned from any future family yule-tide gatherings doesn’t mean you can’t spread your own unique brand of Christmas cheer to other families. Ofcourse not being part of the family makes it more difficult to expose their insecurities:why not expose your own? A favourite of mine is to run away from your long term girlfriend to another state “just for Summer”when she needs you most,and break up with her two week before Christmas from the other side of the country. Then it’s important to get absurdly drunk at the Christmas dinner of the family friends you’re staying with,spill hard liquor on their grandmother,and sing out of tune Disney classics on Singstar with their nieces. To top it off,make sure you then sleep with one of the nieces on Boxing Day and get a photo of her sitting on your lap posted on facebook for your still-grieving ex to see. Not only will your parents be personally horrified,but you’ll have spoiled Christmas for two other families too. The company of strangers Congratulations of getting this far –you’ve worked hard. Now that you can’t go home for Christmas and friends won’t invite you around because you’re a liability,the final stage is to ruin Christmas with people you’ve just met! Book a room in a youth hostel,get drunk and fuck some hideous French girl who doesn’t know enough English to say no! Go back the next year and remind the hostel staff that none of them have moved on their lives! Start fights with the homeless! If you’re in a foreign country,abuse the good intentions of others by tagging along with a friend who you haven’t seen since school,then wage a week long war against their cat. The world is your oyster –people will welcome you into their homes out of charity,and shoo you back out less certain of man’s inherent good nature. Just don’t do anything I wouldn’t do. I like kids and some of them are still innocent,so I wouldn’t want to ruin THEIR Christmas. But,yeah,I have no problem ruining the Christmas of adults that should know better. Although I’m sure I’ll continue to be passive agressive…
